message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being unreasonable for feeling upset about not getting a bagel after picking up my brother and his friends from the airport. Let me break this down step by step. First, I went out of my way to pick them up. I got up early, drove to the airport, and waited around. It was a hassle, but I was happy to do it. However, when I arrived, they weren't there yet. I had to wait, call my brother, and even do a few circles around the airport because I couldn't park. That was frustrating. When they finally got there, they had a big bag of fresh bagels. I was hungry and excited, but when they passed them out, I didn't get one. I jokingly mentioned it, and someone laughed and said no. That made me feel a bit annoyed and upset. Now, my dad got mad at me for even mentioning it. He said I didn't have to get up at 3 am like they did and that they were stressed and had more important things on their minds than getting me a bagel. He also pointed out that airport food is expensive, so I shouldn't expect a free bagel. I know it's just a bagel, but I still feel annoyed. So, is it unreasonable to feel this way? Let me think about the different angles. On one hand, I did a favor for my family, which is important. They were stressed, and maybe they didn't think about getting me a bagel because they were focused on their own needs. Airport food is expensive, so it's understandable they might not want to spend extra money on something for me, especially since I was the one picking them up. On the other hand, I was hungry and excited about the bagels. It's a small thing, but it's also a way of showing appreciation. I felt left out, and that's a valid feeling. It's not about the bagel itself but more about the gesture. Maybe I felt like they didn't consider my needs after I went through the trouble of picking them up. I also wonder if cultural or family dynamics play a role here. In some families, small gestures are important, and not getting one might feel like they didn't care. But in other families, the focus is more on the bigger picture, like getting everyone picked up safely, and small things like bagels aren't a priority. Another thing to consider is communication. Maybe if I had mentioned I was hungry or wanted a bagel before they went to get food, they would have included me. But I didn't, so it's possible they didn't realize I wanted one. It's also possible that they thought I wouldn't want one or that I was okay without it. I also think about the stress of the situation. They were arriving at the airport, which can be stressful, and maybe they were more focused on their own needs and didn't think about mine. It's easy to overlook small things when you're stressed. In the end, I know it's not a big deal, but it's still affecting me. It's important to acknowledge my feelings, even if they seem small to others. Maybe talking it out with my family or finding a way to express my needs next time could help prevent this from happening again. So, considering all these points, I think it's not entirely unreasonable to feel upset. It's a valid feeling, even if it's about something small. However, understanding the other side's perspective can help me feel better about it and maybe improve communication in the future.
